trl_reason: The diffusion-analogy model was calibrated on four Connecticut marshes, validated against observed tide heights on independent dates (max error 0.3 ft), and applied through a GIS/spreadsheet implementation to the real Sybil Creek marsh for gate scenarios; there is no evidence of operational use by regulators or a formally qualified release.

APCTT-C01.quote: Fick’s Law (Fisher and others, 1979) is identical in form to Darcy’s Law and results in the classic onedimensional diffusion equation (eq. 1).
APCTT-C01.note: Derives the model from Darcy's law, continuity and the groundwater tidal-diffusion solution, citing Turner, Todd, Ferris and Fischer.

APCTT-C02.quote: The method was designed to be easily adaptable to other regions of the coast, and it requires only planimetric marsh geometry and the size of the gate opening (leakage) to define the relation between downstream and upstream tidal events.
APCTT-C02.note: Describes applying the model to estimate high-tide heights inland of tide gates in marshes, and how it works from planimetric geometry and calibrated diffusivity.

APCTT-C03.quote: The tide heights were fit by adjusting the diffusivity and thus are in good agreement with the observed heights.
APCTT-C03.note: Calibration results (table 1) show the model reproduces observed high-tide heights and plausible lag times at the four marshes.

APCTT-C04.quote: The calibration of the model was achieved by fitting the best value for diffusivity, given the measured lengths that result in the observed tide heights.
APCTT-C04.note: By analogy: the first model version was tested on existing study datasets (calibration, opening-diffusivity relation, sensitivity to Df and x) with results reported.

APCTT-C05.quote: The method was validated by using the calibrated values for diffusivity to estimate tide heights in Leetes Island marsh, Wilson Cove marsh, and Pine Creek marsh for days not used in the calibration and comparing the estimates against observed heights.
APCTT-C05.note: Validation against real observed tide heights on independent dates in the target marshes; accuracy about 0.1-0.2 ft, max error 0.3 ft (table 2).

APCTT-C06.quote: The method was tested for Sybil Creek in Branford, Conn., by using a GIS application to estimate tide heights at the upland edge of the eastern portion of the Sybil Creek marsh, which is shown on figure 4.
APCTT-C06.note: Working model applied via GIS/spreadsheet to the real Sybil Creek marsh for gate scenarios, checked against one-gate-open observations (within 0.1 ft) and LiDAR.

APCTT-C07.note: No statement that CTDEEP or other intended users actually used the model for real regulatory or restoration decisions; boundary estimates are called approximate.

APCTT-C08.note: No completed, formally qualified release tested against stated requirements.

APCTT-C09.note: No routine operational use over a stated period is reported.

APCTT-C10.note: Accuracy (0.1-0.3 ft) is reported, but no stated requirement or acceptance criterion is given to compare against.

APCTT-C11.quote: The simulations included conditions with the gates closed (existing condition with some leakage of water past the gates which do not close completely in some cases), one gate open, and both gates open.
APCTT-C11.note: Defines the test conditions (tide data source, gate states, dates) and the tested configuration (GIS flow paths, spreadsheet, fixed channel/marsh diffusivities).

APCTT-C12.quote: The method was validated by applying it to the four marshes by using different dates for which observed tide heights were available.
APCTT-C12.note: All calibration, validation and application evidence is about the diffusion-analogy model itself in the named Connecticut marshes.
